pack.title: Horus Voyage
pack.summary: Fly the spaceship Horus to the Sun, the Moon and all eight planets, land and explore each one, then fly out to see the Milky Way.
intro.story1: You are the newest astronaut aboard the Egyptian spaceship Horus. Visit the Sun, the Moon and all eight planets, land and explore each one, then fly out far enough to see our whole galaxy.
intro.story2: Every stop has 3 discoveries, special places and one question. Answer it to earn a stamp in your space passport. Along the way, spacecraft, a comet and golden asteroids are waiting. Dr. Nour is with you on the radio from Mission Control in Cairo.
intro.name: Astronaut name
intro.scale: Distances and sizes here are not to real scale, so the trip stays short.
intro.ctlTouch: Joystick to fly and walk · drag to look · tap a planet to go there
intro.ctlDesk: WASD to fly and walk · drag to look · click a planet to go there
hint.spaceT: Stick to fly where you look · Drag to turn the camera · Pinch to zoom · Tap a planet or pick one from the bar
hint.spaceD: WASD to fly where you look · Q/E down and up · Shift to boost · Drag to turn the camera · Click a planet to go there
hint.rockT: Stick to walk · Jump to feel the gravity · Tap the ground to walk there · walk into the blue and gold lights
hint.rockD: WASD to walk · Space to jump · Shift to run · Click the ground to walk there · walk into the blue and gold lights
hint.gasT: Stick to fly · Up and Down for height · Tap a light to fly to it
hint.gasD: WASD to fly · Space up and C down · Click a light to fly to it
hint.galT: Drag to turn the galaxy · Pinch to zoom · Tap the names to learn
hint.galD: Drag to turn the galaxy · Scroll to zoom · Click the names to learn
mission.title: The Horus mission
mission.done: Every stop visited! Open your passport to see your certificate.
orbit.weight: Someone who weighs 60 kg on Earth would feel like {w} kg here
orbit.gasTeaser: Gas giant: no ground to stand on, so you fly in the clouds.
orbit.sunTeaser: A star of burning gas. No landing, but we can observe it.
space.sunHot: Careful! The Sun is far too hot. I pulled you back.
surf.jumped: You jumped {h} m here · the same jump on Earth: {e} m

surf.tooDeep: The pressure is too high down there! Go back up.

quiz.hint: Not that one. Think back to what you discovered.
r.quizReady: You found all three discoveries! Answer the mission question to earn the stamp.
r.afterQuiz: Well done! What next? The next stop is {n}.
r.afterAll: That is every stamp! Open your passport to see your certificate.
r.welcome: Welcome, {n}! Dr. Nour here, from Mission Control in Cairo. We are in orbit around Earth. Start by landing on Earth, then pick any stop and the autopilot will take you, or press Warp & land to go straight there.
r.comet: A comet is coming our way! Get close before it leaves. You will find it in the log.
ast.name: Golden asteroid
ast.fact: Most asteroids orbit between Mars and Jupiter. The biggest object in the belt, Ceres, is a dwarf planet.
log.title: Voyage log
gal.title: The Milky Way
gal.sub: {n} of 4 places discovered · tap the names
gal.intro: We are now far outside the solar system, looking back at our galaxy, the Milky Way. Distances here are in light-years: a light-year is how far light travels in a year, about 9.5 trillion km.
gal.quizReady: You found all four places in the galaxy! Answer the question to earn the Milky Way stamp.
cert.title: Astronaut certificate
cert.text: This certifies that {name} visited the Sun, the Moon and all eight planets, then flew out to see the Milky Way, aboard Horus.
fact.sun.0: The Sun alone holds about 99.8% of all the mass in the solar system. All the planets together are tiny next to it.
fact.sun.1: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, so the Sun you see is how it looked 8 minutes ago.
fact.sun.2: The Sun’s surface is about 5,500 °C, and about 109 Earths could line up across it.
radio.sun: That’s the Sun, our star. Don’t get any closer! Press Observe and the instruments will take readings.
quiz.sun.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
card.sun:
The Sun alone holds about 99.8% of all the mass in the solar system. All the planets together are tiny next to it.

Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, so the Sun you see is how it looked 8 minutes ago.

The Sun’s surface is about 5,500 °C, and about 109 Earths could line up across it.
fact.mercury.0: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and the smallest planet of all. From here the Sun looks about three times bigger than it does from Earth.
fact.mercury.1: There is almost no air to hold heat, so days reach 430 °C and nights drop to −180 °C.
fact.mercury.2: A year on Mercury is only 88 Earth days, but one sunrise to the next takes 176 Earth days. The day is longer than the year!
radio.mercury: Mercury! The sky is black even in daytime because there is no air. Land and see how big the Sun looks.
quiz.mercury.q: Why does Mercury get so cold at night even though it is closest to the Sun?
quiz.mercury.o0: There is no air to hold the heat
quiz.mercury.o1: It is far from the Sun
card.mercury:
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and the smallest planet of all. From here the Sun looks about three times bigger than it does from Earth.

There is almost no air to hold heat, so days reach 430 °C and nights drop to −180 °C.

A year on Mercury is only 88 Earth days, but one sunrise to the next takes 176 Earth days. The day is longer than the year!
fact.venus.0: Venus is the hottest planet, about 465 °C, even hotter than Mercury. Its thick carbon dioxide air traps the heat. This is called the greenhouse effect.
fact.venus.1: The air pressure on Venus is about 90 times Earth’s, like being about 900 metres under the sea.
fact.venus.2: Venus spins backwards and very slowly: one spin takes 243 Earth days, longer than its 225-day year. The Sun rises in the west there.
radio.venus: Venus. Your suit is built for this heat, but don’t stay too long. The clouds here contain sulfuric acid!
quiz.venus.q: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury even though it is farther from the Sun?
quiz.venus.o0: Its thick air traps the heat
quiz.venus.o1: It is closer to the Sun
quiz.venus.o2: Volcanoes erupt there all the time
card.venus:
Venus is the hottest planet, about 465 °C, even hotter than Mercury. Its thick carbon dioxide air traps the heat. This is called the greenhouse effect.

The air pressure on Venus is about 90 times Earth’s, like being about 900 metres under the sea.

Venus spins backwards and very slowly: one spin takes 243 Earth days, longer than its 225-day year. The Sun rises in the west there.
fact.earth.0: Earth is the only planet we know of that has life.
fact.earth.1: About 71% of Earth’s surface is covered by water, which is why it looks blue from space.
fact.earth.2: Earth’s air, mostly nitrogen and oxygen, and its magnetic field protect life from harmful radiation from the Sun.
radio.earth: Welcome home! You will land in Giza, next to the pyramids. Take a breath of real air.
quiz.earth.q: How much of Earth’s surface is covered by water?
card.earth:
Earth is the only planet we know of that has life.

About 71% of Earth’s surface is covered by water, which is why it looks blue from space.

Earth’s air, mostly nitrogen and oxygen, and its magnetic field protect life from harmful radiation from the Sun.
fact.moon.0: In 1969 Apollo 11 landed on the Moon and Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on it. By 1972, 12 astronauts had walked on the Moon.
fact.moon.1: There is no air or wind on the Moon, so astronauts’ footprints can last for millions of years.
fact.moon.2: The Moon always shows Earth the same face, because it spins once in the same time it takes to orbit Earth.
radio.moon: The Moon! Gravity here is one sixth of Earth’s. Try jumping and see how high you go.
quiz.moon.q: How many astronauts walked on the Moon during the Apollo missions?
card.moon:
In 1969 Apollo 11 landed on the Moon and Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on it. By 1972, 12 astronauts had walked on the Moon.

There is no air or wind on the Moon, so astronauts’ footprints can last for millions of years.

The Moon always shows Earth the same face, because it spins once in the same time it takes to orbit Earth.
fact.mars.0: Mars is red because its dust and rocks are full of iron oxide, which is rust.
fact.mars.1: Mars has the biggest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, about 22 km high, roughly two and a half times Mount Everest.
fact.mars.2: A day on Mars is just a bit longer than Earth’s, about 24 hours and 40 minutes.
radio.mars: Mars, the red planet. Robots got here before us. Look for one!
quiz.mars.o0: There is rust in its dust
quiz.mars.o2: It is covered in red plants
card.mars:
Mars is red because its dust and rocks are full of iron oxide, which is rust.

Mars has the biggest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, about 22 km high, roughly two and a half times Mount Everest.

A day on Mars is just a bit longer than Earth’s, about 24 hours and 40 minutes.
fact.jupiter.0: Jupiter is the biggest planet in the solar system. More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.
fact.jupiter.1: Jupiter is a gas giant, mostly hydrogen and helium, with no solid surface to stand on.
fact.jupiter.2: The Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth, and scientists have watched it for more than 150 years.
radio.jupiter: Jupiter, king of the planets. There is no ground, so you will fly with your jetpack in the clouds. Look up to see its moons!
quiz.jupiter.q: Why can’t you stand on Jupiter?
card.jupiter:
Jupiter is the biggest planet in the solar system. More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

Jupiter is a gas giant, mostly hydrogen and helium, with no solid surface to stand on.

The Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth, and scientists have watched it for more than 150 years.
fact.saturn.0: Saturn’s rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock, some as small as sand grains and some as big as houses.
fact.saturn.1: Saturn is less dense than water. In a big enough bathtub, it would float!
fact.saturn.2: Saturn’s largest moon, Titan, has thick air and lakes of liquid methane.
radio.saturn: Saturn! Look up from inside the clouds and you will see the rings across the sky.
quiz.saturn.q: What are Saturn’s rings made of?
card.saturn:
Saturn’s rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock, some as small as sand grains and some as big as houses.

Saturn is less dense than water. In a big enough bathtub, it would float!

Saturn’s largest moon, Titan, has thick air and lakes of liquid methane.
fact.uranus.0: Uranus spins lying on its side, tilted about 98 degrees, like a rolling ball.
fact.uranus.1: Uranus is an ice giant, and its blue-green colour comes from methane gas.
fact.uranus.2: Uranus has the coldest air of any planet, down to about −224 °C. A year there lasts 84 Earth years.
radio.uranus: Uranus, the ice giant. It is colder here than you can imagine.
quiz.uranus.q: What is strange about how Uranus spins?
quiz.uranus.o1: It does not spin at all
card.uranus:
Uranus spins lying on its side, tilted about 98 degrees, like a rolling ball.

Uranus is an ice giant, and its blue-green colour comes from methane gas.

Uranus has the coldest air of any planet, down to about −224 °C. A year there lasts 84 Earth years.
fact.neptune.0: Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system, more than 2,000 km/h.
fact.neptune.1: Neptune was found with maths! In 1846 scientists worked out where it was from the way Uranus moved, before anyone saw it.
fact.neptune.2: A year on Neptune lasts 165 Earth years. It finished its first full orbit since its discovery only in 2011.
radio.neptune: Neptune, the last planet. Hold on, the winds here are faster than anything you have seen!
quiz.neptune.o0: Scientists predicted it with maths first
card.neptune:
Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system, more than 2,000 km/h.

Neptune was found with maths! In 1846 scientists worked out where it was from the way Uranus moved, before anyone saw it.

A year on Neptune lasts 165 Earth years. It finished its first full orbit since its discovery only in 2011.
quiz.galaxy.q: How long does the Sun take to go once around the centre of the galaxy?
lm.mercury.0.fact: This crater looks like the Caloris Basin, one of the largest impact craters in the solar system, about 1,550 km wide. A huge space rock made it billions of years ago.
lm.mercury.1.fact: Inside craters near Mercury’s poles where sunlight never reaches, scientists found water ice. The planet closest to the Sun has ice!
lm.venus.0.fact: Venus has more volcanoes than any other planet in the solar system. One of the best known, Maat Mons, is about 8 km high.
lm.venus.1.fact: This looks like the Soviet Venera 13 lander. In 1982 it landed here and kept working for only 127 minutes before the heat and pressure destroyed it.
lm.earth.0.fact: The Great Pyramid is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
lm.earth.1.fact: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world, about 6,650 km long. Without it, ancient Egyptian civilisation could not have grown.
lm.moon.0.fact: This looks like an Apollo landing craft and the flag the astronauts planted. In reality, the strong sunlight has faded the flag’s colours.
lm.moon.1.fact: From the Moon, Earth looks about four times wider than the Moon looks from Earth. The famous Earthrise photo was taken from lunar orbit in 1968.
lm.mars.0.fact: This robot looks like Perseverance, exploring Mars since 2021. It drills into rocks looking for signs of tiny life that may have lived here long ago.
lm.mars.1.fact: Mars has dust devils, spinning columns of dust like small tornadoes. Some grow several kilometres tall.
lm.jupiter.0.fact: Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, is the most volcanically active place in the solar system.
lm.jupiter.1.fact: Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system, bigger than the planet Mercury.
lm.saturn.0.fact: Saturn’s rings stretch up to about 280,000 km from the planet, but the main rings are typically only about 10 metres thick!
lm.saturn.1.fact: At Saturn’s north pole there is a giant six-sided storm, wider than Earth itself.
lm.uranus.0.fact: Uranus has 13 known rings, and because the planet lies on its side, its rings look like they stand upright.
lm.uranus.1.fact: Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus, in 1986. It went on to visit Neptune in 1989.
lm.neptune.0.fact: In 1989 Voyager 2 photographed a giant storm here called the Great Dark Spot. Later it disappeared!
lm.neptune.1.fact: Triton, Neptune’s largest moon, orbits backwards and has geysers that shoot out gas.
craft.iss.fact: The International Space Station circles Earth about every 90 minutes, about 400 km up, and astronauts have lived aboard without a break since 2000.
craft.jwst.fact: The James Webb Space Telescope launched in December 2021. Its gold mirror is 6.5 metres wide, and it sits about 1.5 million km from Earth.
craft.voyager.fact: Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and is the farthest human-made object. In 2012 it left the bubble the Sun blows around us and entered interstellar space.
craft.comet.fact: Comets are balls of ice and dust. Near the Sun the ice turns to gas and makes a long tail that always points away from the Sun.
gal.center.fact: At the centre of the galaxy sits a giant black hole called Sagittarius A*, about 4 million times the mass of the Sun.
gal.sun.fact: You are here! The Sun sits in a small arm called the Orion Arm, about 26,000 light-years from the centre. It takes about 230 million years to go once around it.
gal.edge.fact: The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across and holds between 100 and 400 billion stars.
gal.andromeda.fact: Andromeda is the nearest large galaxy, about 2.5 million light-years away. The light we see from it left long before modern humans existed.
card.galaxy:
We are now far outside the solar system, looking back at our galaxy, the Milky Way. Distances here are in light-years: a light-year is how far light travels in a year, about 9.5 trillion km.

You are here! The Sun sits in a small arm called the Orion Arm, about 26,000 light-years from the centre. It takes about 230 million years to go once around it.

item.gravity.q: Gravity on the Moon is about one sixth of Earth’s. Someone who weighs 60 kg on Earth would feel like how many kg on the Moon?
